candidate_relations.rationale: The ordinary-repair tests independently verify deterministic projection rebuild from valid history and exceptional recovery on invalid history, directly strengthening the ordinary-repair contract.

Installer tests that managed drift and post-activation failures stop or restore safely strengthen the Rupi update/recovery test proposition that update reuses the installer primitive, managed drift stops mutation, and project-owned state is preserved.

The project-identity bridge tests showing v2 identity as valid bootstrap state and exact first-admission reuse strengthen the compatibility amendment that v1-to-v2 migration occurs only from explicit complete v2 identity.

The mutation runtime's explicit proposal revalidation and proposal/approval validation before state transitions strengthen the bounded-authority-grant contract requiring immediately-before revalidation and independent apply-time validation.

The accepted-release greenfield retest shows bootstrap creates only minimum project-owned structure and no canonical or authority state, strengthening the Rupi install/bootstrap handoff boundary that authority setup remains outside lifecycle bootstrap.

The Rupi authority-flow tests show authority setup requires distinct protected ceremonies and creates no activation or semantic state, strengthening the handoff proposition that protected authority setup stays outside install/bootstrap lifecycle handling.

The installer tests' preservation or restoration of the previous install on validation failures independently strengthen the Rupi failed-update observation that failures roll back and do not report false success.
